Circus Lions/OPERATION SPIRIT OF FREEDOM

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
EMPTYING THE CAGES OF PERU'S CIRCUS. THE REMARKABLE JOURNEY OF 33 LIONS BACK TO AFRICA

Summary:
OPERATION SPIRIT OF FREEDOM

Imagine emptying an entire countries circus animals and giving them back their freedom? That is what has just taken place in Peru and South Africa is part of that.




Further information:
Flashback to 2008. President of Animal defenders Jan Creamer in the Peruvian Congress pressed for a ban on animals in circuses in Peru. It came on the back of an undercover investigation on the horrors of animals in Peruvian circuses which mobilized massive public support. But it took four long years before Peru banned wild animals in circuses in November 2012.
And since then ADI has been going from circus to circus freeing animals and working incredibly hard behind the scenes to find suitable homes for the animals. Enter Savannah Heuser – a young girl in her twenties who inherited a game farm in the Waterberg. When Savannah was just a few months old her father died tragically and she was raised by her mother Minunette. Savannah is now in her early twenties, a serious and thoughtful young woman who has a very clear idea of how she wants things done. They are both feisty women and they don’t suffer fools or hangers on and there are many of these in the wild life world. There are two tigers on the property and a small pride of rescued lions. One of the lions comes from a wealthy palace in Saudi Arabia.

Then one day Minunette got a call- would they consider taking in 33 former circus lions from Peru? Minunette and Savannah originally said no. Taking on 33 lions who cannot hunt for themselves is not only expensive it’s a long term commitment.
But Savannah is one of those people who lives her life by the Ghandi dictum: Be the change you want to see in the world and so they began to negotiate with ADI. If ADI could fit the bill for the enclosures and the food, they were happy to provide the land and the staff to feed the lions.
But its never that simple and back in South America Jan Creamer President of ADI has been working tirelessly to find not only the backing but also the means to get the lions back to AFRICA. And here in SA it took a long time to get all the permits necessary.

Finally on Saturday at 09 30 am, the animals will touch down in the cargo section of OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL – before they begin the long journey to the Waterberg. Its estimated they will arrive just as the sun is setting but ADI are determined that they will work late into the night to get all the animals out of their crates as soon as they get there.

Carte Blanche joins this massive lion rescue and brings you all the action of this good news story.

Press Release:


Operation: Spirit of Freedom
It was a huge operation, returning 33 circus lions from South America back to Africa. The rescue thrust 19-year-old Savannah Heuser into the limelight as the lions were released onto African soil at the sanctuary she founded four years ago. Join Carte Blanche as we witness lions that have never seen trees before embrace their new surroundings and take their first tentative steps outside their confinement.


Script:


Final Script 33 Lions/ operation spirit of Freedom

Commentary One
She was only 13 when Savannah Heuser dreamt of a sanctuary for lions that could not survive in the wild.

Savannah Heuser Founder Emoya Big Cat Sanctuary
We were never meant to pet lions, we were never meant to ride them, and never meant to do anything that they don’t want to do. These animals don’t have a voice and I want to be a voice for them

Commentary Two
Savannah inherited a farm in the Waterberg. Now a reserved nineteen- year old, her dreams have taken shape quietly, out of the limelight, where she co-founded Emoya big cat sanctuary

Savannah
Emoya existed for 4 years without anyone knowing about us, we like to basically stay quiet and stay out of the drama because I think there is enough of it already

Commentary Three
But this week she was thrust into the limelight as 33 circus lions, rescued from Columbia and Peru made their way across the Atlantic, in the biggest airlift of lions, ever undertaken

Savannah
These cats come from such horrific conditions – brutally declawed – teeth literally beaten out of the animals- a few lions here that were only fed chicken feet. That is cruelty

Commentary Four
Each lion in these crates has witnessed the worst side of our own nature

Up sound lion growls with ball

Commentary Five
But 26 years ago these circus animals finally had two people fighting for them, when Jan Creamer and Tim Phillips founded Animal Defenders International or ADI

Jan Creamer President Animal Defenders International
these animals are not there for entertainment. When we first released the evidence of the suffering we got bans in five countries in America – over 30 countries banned the use of animals in circuses

Commentary Six
They have worked with governments to change laws, faced down angry mobs,
rescued lions with riot police, but slowly, they are emptying circus cages across South America

UP sound Uno Momento! Momento!
Tim Phillips Co founder and VP ADI
We have completely rescued the circus’s, of every animal in Bolivia and Peru now

Commentary seven
It took 18 months, but they have rescued around 100 animals including this bear that had lost all its hair

Tim
During the rescue we have seized animals all over Peru and they have been in circus sometimes a 1000 miles apart. We have been through snow storms – we have been through everything on this rescue – its been a rescue on a very very big scale

MUSIC MONTAGE TRAVELLING

Commentary Eight
The Columbian nine, are lions from Bocaramanga, a city in Northern Columbia.
They first travelled to Bogota, then on to Lima in Peru, where they joined the other 24 lions.

Plane flies

Last Saturday they arrived at OR Tambo and were greeted by a frenzy of international and local photographers. These lions would have spent almost four days in their crates

CLICK CLICK CLICK

Commentary nine
It was the culmination of months of planning by Savannah and her mother Minunette

Savannah
My mother is the most supportive person I know – she always tells people I am the brainchild behind this but the absolute truth is that I couldn’t have done any of this without her

Minunette
savannah and I were always close. I was a single mother for most of savannah’s life .. passion that started the sanctuary 13 when we started– I fell in love with the lions too

Commentary Ten
The lions come from 7 different families, and each lion was positioned next to a family member in the plane, and then again later on the donated trucks. OR Tambo’s Cargo section, vibrated as the Lima boys, tried to out do the Columbians

UP SOUND ROARING




Commentary eleven
By Midnight the cold front was biting, and tarpaulins were pulled over the trucks to protect the older lions. Freedom was still a six- hour drive to Limpopo, but finally these animals left a city for the very last time in their lives

HOOT HOOT

Trucks travel night music and into gate

As the first lions arrived at their new home Minunette hadn’t slept for about 30 hours

Minunette Heuser
I thought what have we done but in a good way – 33 circus cats – it’s a massive undertaking especially for a private owned sanctuary

ROAR ROAR ROAR

Commentary twelve
Travelling with the lions from Columbia was Yani Mateus. She has worked with them for the last 18 months. Initially they were very aggressive

Yani Mateus
If you try to get close to them they jump, they push.

Commentary thirteen
But with love and good food, that’s all changed

Yanni
Ya they are my family of course.

Commentary fourteen
Lifting the lions was a bit of a boer maak n plan affair, but it worked to get the lions positioned one by one at these bonding camps with their family members. They will be held in the smaller camps and only later released into the much larger enclosures

Minunette
most of the lions never had physical contact with their family members, so we need to see which relationships work out and which don’t work out- some of these lions will need surgery,– third reason – 9 females – no breeding policy – females can’t be in same enclosure as the males

Commentary fifteen
The Columbians were the first to be released as they had been in their crates the longest

MInunette
What will be interesting to see how they react to trees – they don’t know trees


Commentary sixteen
This is Iron, he was first lion out ….but cages have been his life and he wants back in …

Commentary seventeen
One by one the lions were released.

This is Zeus

Savannah lifts cage

Commentary eighteen
The Columbian boys spent the morning working out their differences

Commentary nineteen
But the Columbian girls were unimpressed

Commentary twenty
Smith is a Peruvian lion. And the most notorious of the thirty- three

Tim
His life symbolizes the life of a circus animal

Commentary twenty- one
Smith lived in cage about the size of a vehicle. He has no mane because he was castrated. Then he was declawed

Jan
When we say declaw – cut off the toes and knuckle – later on very painful – foot starts to collapse

Commentary twenty- two
Smith was used in a routine where he was forced to jump over a member of the public

Tim
one day they put him in the ring / trainer not in the ring – smith dragged her around and around the ring/ kill this lion and we met with the minister for 6 hours that day and we got smith out of that circus. he was stuck in a circus in South America and people wanted him killed – not many get out of that situation alive

Commentary twenty three
For the people the lions were the star attraction, but for the lions, the trees won hands down

Tim
This is the pay off off all the hard work, this is decades work gone into freeing these animals. These lions have never rubbed against a tree before. That is just magical



Commentary twenty four
Its going to cost around R2000 a day to feed the lions, but when Savannah sees this once abused circus lion roll in the sand, nothing else seems to matter

Savannah laughs
That is what makes it all worthwhile. We are all tired our feet ..we just want to numb them – but you forget about everything when you see a lion react that way

THE END 10 02

PROMO ONE 10 seconds

The joy of Trees for the first time, for the newly released circus lions from South America

PROMO TWO
After enduring years of abuse, nine circus lions from the Columbian Andes and 24 lions from Peru were airlifted across the Atlantic last week and began their new life in the African Bush. We track their incredible journey

PROMO THREE
Savannah Heuser was only 13 when she dreamt of owning a sanctuary for big cats that could not look after themselves in the wild.
Savannah
These animals don’t have a voice and I want to be a voice for them
